projects.title: Starship Booster Cryo Proof Tooling
projects.summary: Responsible Engineer for the 13,000+ component assembly that seals Starship Booster's 33 engine feedlines during Cryo Proof — the last full-vehicle test before engines go on.

points.text: Responsible Engineer for the 13,000+ component assembly sealing Starship Booster's 33 engine feedlines during Cryo Proof.

Re-designed the tooling to seal properly with a high-flow gaseous oxygen test assembly, a drain manifold for post-test cryo removal, and gas system ports enabling decay checks and transducer testing with the Checkouts team.
Directed $800,000 in machined part procurement, running daily vendor calls to ensure timely, print-conforming delivery.
Ran FEA on max-pressure blow-off load cases to validate structural and sealing performance under Cryo Proof loading.

Oversaw up to 25 technicians during subassembly build and vehicle integration, dispositioning issues on the floor, designing lineside parts storage, and physically integrating tooling on-vehicle to resolve fit issues firsthand.
Ran a daily stand-up and authored a daily status email to 80+ stakeholders, driving alignment across organizations.
Saved over 1,100 production hours per vehicle through design rate improvements, streamlined planning, and better storage.

projects.note: Design work performed at SpaceX is proprietary — no CAD, drawings, part numbers, or hardware imagery are shown.

projects.title: Starship Weld Cell, Lift Tooling & Flight Retrofits
projects.summary: Built a new weld-focused subassembly cell for a high-pressure propulsion manifold, designed the lift and access tooling around it, and owned five retrofitted flight parts modelled from as-built CAD.

points.text: Designed and built a new weld-focused subassembly build cell for a high-pressure propulsion manifold on the Starship vehicle.
Designed fixture tooling to fit up endpoint flanges on tubes, using GD&T to hold tolerance across the 9-meter-long weld cell.
Designed a lift tool rated to 1,100 lbs and proof-tested to 2× working load limit for safe handling of propulsion assemblies.
Designed a tool improving work access and integration for aft flap torque frames on the rocket, saving 50 labor hours per vehicle.
Owned five retrofitted flight parts, modeling precise as-built CAD assemblies to manufacture off-nominal parts on assembly.
Worked with suppliers to coordinate over $50,000 in purchases, delivering tools lineside on a tight schedule.
Supported over 5,000 hours of technician labor, resolving issues on the floor and managing up to 16 technicians at once.

projects.title: Brake Rotors & Mounts
projects.summary: Designed the most reliable brake rotor possible within FSAE regulations — trading a little pad wear for de-gassing and debris clearing, and keeping a weight-optimised aluminium mount thermally isolated from the steel disc.

points.text: The most reliable brake rotor possible per FSAE regulations and driver safety — not the lightest one.
4140 steel rotors, titanium brake buttons, and a 7075 aluminium rotor mount.
Slots de-gas the pad interface and clear debris, at the cost of slightly increased pad wear.
Structural hand calculations from maximum kinetic energy absorption per FSAE rules and brake bias set the minimum thickness for the fully restrained temperature-delta case.
Titanium brake buttons act as the thermal choke point between the steel rotor and the weight-optimised aluminium mount.
The mount interfaces directly with the differential bolts; caliper selection came out of the same brake-bias study.
FEA validated the structural integrity and temperature tolerance of both the rotor and its mount.

projects.title: Rear Wheel Hub Assembly
projects.summary: Designed the lightest reliable rear wheel hub allowed by FSAE regulations — designed for manufacturing, with thread engagement sized analytically and the final geometry validated in Ansys.

points.text: The lightest reliable wheel hub possible per FSAE regulations, designed for manufacturing from the start.
7075-T6 aluminium — the added cost is worth the reliability gained in yield strength over 6061-T6.
Hub nut thread length calculated from bolt tensile stress area and nut thread shear area, prioritising reliability alongside weight savings.
Hub geometry validated with Ansys finite element analysis against maximum cornering and braking load cases.

projects.title: Carbon Pushrod & Swept Control Arms
projects.summary: Re-engineered the wishbone and pushrod assembly to minimise mass and packaging volume while eliminating clearance conflicts at maximum heave and roll — cutting 5 lbs of suspension weight — then fabricated the set by hand.

points.text: Reduce weight, decrease packaging size, and minimise clearance issues with the other wheel pickup points at maximum heave or roll.
Cut suspension weight by 5 lbs by placing the pushrod mounting gussets directly on the apex and switching the pushrod material from steel to carbon fiber.
Validated apex fatigue strength in SolidWorks FEA so pushrod and wheel forces would not cause failures after repeated load cycles — 38.6 ksi peak von Mises at the upper apex.
Lathed steel tube stock to length and diameter, manually milled steel plugs, hand-tapped the control arms to accept rod ends, and hand-painted each wishbone.

projects.title: Discrete Ride Height Adjustment
projects.summary: A shim-based pushrod adjuster, inspired by Formula 1 practice and not previously seen in FSAE, letting trackside engineers make exact ride-height changes in seconds instead of counting turns on an opposite-thread pushrod.

points.text: The previous system relied on rotating a pushrod with opposite threads — inaccurate and time consuming.
A mechanism allowing exact ride-height changes with minimal disassembly.
Designed in SolidWorks, heavily inspired by Formula 1 technology that had not previously been seen in FSAE.
Lets engineers quickly insert or remove shims from the pushrods in a competition environment to change aerodynamic behaviour or roll center.
SolidWorks FEA on the discrete adjustment attachment validated its structural integrity under pushrod load.
6061 aluminium — the mechanism added only 0.7 lb to the weight of the entire car.

projects.title: Wheel Bearing Selection
projects.summary: Simulated dynamic load cases in SKF SimPro Quick to select rear wheel bearings optimised for fatigue life and load capacity — the lightest bearing that still cleared static and dynamic safety factors, saving 0.8 lb.

points.text: Find the lightest bearing with acceptable static and dynamic safety factors under maximum cornering force loads at the tires.
Built a wheel hub assembly simulation in SKF SimPro Quick with maximum tire loads applied, then swept every bearing within the acceptable dimensional envelope for fatigue life and load capacity.
Collaborated with Powertrain to set bearing ID parameters from the selected tripod bearings on the half shaft.
Simulated power loss across the operating wheel-speed range to confirm the selection did not trade weight for drag.
Selected the SKF 71817 ACDGB/VQ253 angular contact ball bearing — 0.8 pounds saved.

projects.title: Motion-Capture Integration for Swarm Manufacturing
projects.summary: Integrated an infrared motion-capture camera system with a robotic arm and its driver software in Python, enabling real-time position tracking for swarm manufacturing research.

points.text: Connected an infrared motion-capture camera system to a robotic arm and its driver software using Python and the NatNet SDK.
Enabled real-time position tracking to support swarm manufacturing research in the lab.
Presented findings in front of UT research faculty.

projects.title: Adjustable Hose-Carrying Assembly
projects.summary: A chain-linkage carrier that safely walks hydraulic hoses from their storage position to the position of operation on a geotechnical drill rig, driven along a sketched path so the assembly can be re-pathed without re-mating parts.

points.text: Safely transport hydraulic hoses from the storage position to the position of operation on a geotechnical drill rig.
Designed a chain linkage part with rotational freedom at the mating interface.
Created a path sketch for the chain-link assembly to navigate the drill rig and avoid interferences.
Mated the chain link assembly so one end is fixed while the other travels freely along the sketch path.
